description_full: Golar LNG Limited designs, converts, owns, and operates marine infrastructure for the liquefaction of natural gas. The company operates in two segments, FLNG, and Corporate and Other. It engages in the regasification, storage, and liquefied natural gas (LNG) carrier transportation operations; operation of floating liquefaction natural gas (FLNG) vessels or projects; transportation of LNG carriers; and vessel management activities. The company was founded in 1946 and is headquartered in Hamilton, Bermuda.

culture_narrative: Employs approximately 500 people. Revenue per employee of $787K ranks in the below the sector median among Energy peers. Stock-based compensation of $13K per employee reflects an ownership culture.
financial_summary: Golar LNG Limited is a mid-cap energy business with a $4.4B market cap on $394M of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +14% over the past three years and +14% annually across the full decade, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder.
Returns on capital run at 3% against a 8% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests.
On the balance sheet, debt is heavy at 10.9× net debt/EBITDA, and leverage like that is what turns a bad year into a permanent loss, and interest coverage runs at 3.0×.

Shareholder yield of 2.3% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insiders hold 5.9% of the shares, and within its sector the business captures 2.3× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
